Veesala Indra Prabha vs The State Of Telangana And 7 Others
on 7 June, 2024

entities.text: Veesala Indra Prabha vs The State Of Telangana And 7 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: Nagesh Bheemapaka
Bench: Nagesh Bheemapaka
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka
 Writ Petition No. 44360 Of 2023
Order:

Petitioner claims to be the absolute owner and possessor of house property bearing Municipal No.16-1-523/6, admeasuring 113.5 square yards situated at Sayeedabad, Hyderabad, by virtue of the gift settlement deed dated 26.06.2020.

Initially, Municipal Number of the subject premises was 16-1-523/6 and later on, three Mulgies & Staircase were constructed facing the main road, as such,
Municipal Number was changed to 16-1-523/6/1 to 3.

It is stated, the Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, GHMC, Hyderabad, in the process of widening the road leading from Chanchalaguda to Madanapet to 100 feet, took steps to acquire properties including subject property.

As per the Notification dated 31.05.2021, petitioner's property to an extent of 97 square yards was affected and subsequently Award was passed in respect of the aforesaid land and the structure standing thereon i.e. Mulgies and Staircase
have been demolished and presently, there is a left over land of nearly 16 square yards.
It is the case of petitioner that as her husband has no other source of income, even the small strip of land is useful for their livelihood.

While so, it is stated that the staff of Respondents 6 to 8 - Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (TSSPDCL) started raising pillars for installation of two electrical transformers in the left over place.

entities.text: Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Company Limited
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, petitioner approached Respondents 3 and 4 - Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (for short, 'the Corporation'), but of no avail; thereafter, they also approached Respondents 6 to 8 who have categorically stated that work is being carried out on the site identified by Respondents 3 and 4 and that they would not stop the work which is being undertaken in left over land of her property.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner K. Jamali submits that respondents have resorted to the atrocious act of installing two electrical transformers in a private property which is apparent from the deplorable actions of the staff of Respondents 6 to 8.
According to learned counsel, there are other government properties available adjacent to the subject left over land where two electrical transformers can be installed.

Hence, submits that learned counsel that a direction may be issued to the 5th respondent to restrain Respondents 6 to 8 from proceeding with installation of two electrical transformers in petitioner's left over property.

sentences.text: The 3rd respondent - Deputy Commissioner, GHMC filed the counter stating that there were already existing transformers on the margin of the road from long time.
The respondent Corporation has proposed expansion of road to 100 feet width and for the said purpose, land abutting the said road has been acquired from many owners of said land.
It is stated that earlier transformers were dismantled as they were erected along the old road, but after expansion, they were shifted to road margin.

The Corporation demarcated the land where the transformers have to be erected along the new road margin and as per their demarcation, piller and plinth beam have been constructed above 6 feet from the ground and transformers shall be erected on the said construction.

It is stated that the Corporation initiated action as per the Notification dated 31.05.2021; an extent of 97 square yards is affected under the private road widening and subsequently, award was also passed in respect of the aforesaid land and compensation was paid to petitioner and mulgies and staircase were demolished and there is left over land of nearly 16 square yards.
It is stated that at present, new transformers are being erected by Respondents 6 to 8 above 6 feet from the ground level to prevent any untoward incidents.
Transformers have been erected on the road margin as demarcated by the Corporation duly following the due process of law and there is no deliberate or intentional Act on the part of the Corporation.
3. The 7th respondent - Assistant Divisional Engineer, TSSPDCL filed the counter-affidavit stating that there were existing transformers on the margin of the road from the long time.
The Corporation had proposed expansion of road to 100 feet width and for the said purpose, land abutting the said road was acquired from many owners.
It is stated that earlier transformers were dismantled as they were erected along the old road and after expansion, they have to be shifted to the road margin.

The officials of the Corporation have demarcated the land where the transformers have to be erected along the new road margin and as per their demarcation, pillar and plinth beam have been constructed above 6 feet from the ground and transformers shall be erected on the said construction.
At present, all the new transformers are being erected above 6 feet from the ground level to prevent any untoward accidents.
The contention of the petitioner that the transformers are being erected in the land owned by her is not true.
The photographs being filed herewith go to prove that the transformers are being erected on the road margin.

It is further stated that transformers have to be erected immediately and power supply has to be provided for all the consumers which was being serviced by the earlier transformer and necessary work has been undertaken to complete the same at the earliest.
4.
Petitioner filed the reply-affidavit to the counter filed by the 7th respondent.
It is stated therein that there were existing transformers on the road margin prior to road widening, but at that point of time also, no transformers was there in front of the subject property.

It is submitted that Writ Petition was filed against Respondents 6 to 8 after they started civil works for installing two electrical transformers in her property for the purpose of construction without following due process of Law.

Petitioner is not in the know whether earlier transformers were dismantled and presently,
no road margin is in existence as in the process of road widening only properties abutting the road have been dismantled and on the land acquired, no road has been laid, as such, the contention of the Veesala Indra Prabha vs The State Of Telangana And 7 Others on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32804111/
2

entities.text: Veesala Indra Prabha vs The State Of Telangana And 7 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7th respondent that there exists road margin is absolutely baseless and vehemently denied.

It is stated that the civil work for installing transformers has been undertaken within a distance of 4.5 feet from her backside wall which is well within the left over land and the width of the left over land is nearly 6 feet, as such the assertion of the 7th respondent that transformers are to be installed on the road margin as identified by the Corporation is totally false and they should not be allowed to continue with the process of installing transformers in a private property.

It is further stated that the stand of the 7th respondent that after verification and demarcation of land by the officials of the Corporation, where transformers have to be erected along the new road margin and as per their demarcation, pillar and plinth beam have been constructed above 6 feet from the ground and transformers shall be erected on the said construction may not be relevant as the 7th respondent has not clearly answered her contention that transformer is to be installed in left over property and has shifted the blame on the Corporation on the ground that the latter had identified the road margin.
It is finally stated that Respondents 6 to 8 are trying to install two electrical transformers in her property without following due process of Law.

5. Heard Sri Praveen Kumar Veerjala, learned Standing Counsel for the Corporation as well as Sri R.
Vinod Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for TSSPDCL.
6.

The simple and lone case of petitioner is that the Corporation had acquired 97 square yards and still, there is 16 square yards of left over land and the respondent authorities have been installing two electrical transformers in her private property of 16 square yards.

On the contrary, the stand of the Corporation as well as TSSPDCL is that already existing transformers were dismantled as they were erected along the old road, but after expansion, they were shifted to road margin.

The Corporation demarcated the land where the transformers have to be erected along the new road margin and as per their demarcation, pillar and plinth beam have been constructed above 6 feet from the ground and transformers shall be erected on the said construction.
In view of the above facts and circumstances, whether transformers are being erected in the private property of petitioner or along the new road side is a disputed question of fact.
It has to be decided based on the evidence to be placed by both the parties.
This Court cannot conduct an enquiry into the same while exercising its jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution.
Even if the case of petitioner is taken as true, the remedy lies elsewhere but not before this Court.

The Writ Petition is therefore,
liable to be dismissed as this Court cannot go into the disputed questions of fact.
7. The Writ Petition is accordingly, dismissed.
However, liberty is given to petitioner to work out her remedies in an appropriate forum.
No costs.
8. Consequently, the miscellaneous Applications, if any shall stand closed.

NAGESH BHEEMAPAKA, J 07th June 2024 ksld Veesala Indra Prabha vs The State Of Telangana And 7 Others on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32804111/
